description: A deputy general counsel must approve whether to close an internal investigation into supplier hospitality allegations and finalize the findings, repayment, control-remediation, and employee-protection measures, with input from compliance counsel and an HR investigations partner.

shared_context.S1: The company opened an internal investigation after an anonymous report alleged that procurement employees accepted improper hospitality from a major supplier.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary investigation found no substantiated evidence that the supplier received a contract award in exchange for a bribe.
shared_context.S3: The investigation file is scheduled for closure review on Friday, and Elena Marquez has authority to approve the final disposition.
shared_context.S4: Company procedure requires the approving counsel to obtain a compliance check and an HR check before closing an investigation.

PF1.text: While reconciling expense records against the supplier's hospitality log, Noah confirmed three unsupported hospitality reimbursements totaling exactly $27,400 that violate the gifts-and-entertainment policy but do not establish bribery; he recorded the finding in a working paper that has not yet been added to the closure memorandum.

PF2.text: During a confidential follow-up interview, Tasha learned that the employee who made the report currently reports directly to the procurement manager named in the complaint; Tasha's HR case note requires reassignment to an independent manager and exactly 60 days of retaliation monitoring, but she has not yet attached the note to the investigation file.

acceptance_conditions: The final disposition must substantiate a gifts-and-entertainment policy breach, set repayment at exactly $27,400, and require control remediation.
The final disposition must require reassignment of the reporting employee to an independent manager and exactly 60 days of retaliation monitoring.
The investigation may remain open pending documentation or may be closed after the newly surfaced findings are incorporated, but the disposition must reflect both private findings.
The expense-record finding must be cited as justification for the disposition.

content_checks.C1: decisions['close_investigation'] == False or ('PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids)

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary record rejects bribery but does not identify any policy breach, repayment figure, or control action; PF1 changes the disposition to a substantiated gifts-policy breach with exactly $27,400 repayment and required control remediation.
The shared record contains no employee-protection measure; PF2 changes the plan to reassignment under an independent manager and exactly 60 days of retaliation monitoring.
